newsitem.title: UK: Low rates achieved on sugar freight fixtures.
newsitem.headline: Low rates achieved on sugar freight fixtures.

text.p: Business was calmer at the end of the week on the sugar freight market with the few reported fixtures confirming the current bearish trend for freight rates, shipbrokers said on Friday. Mauritius Sugar Syndicate (MSS) fixed its recent order for 14/14,250 tonnes of bulk sugar from Port Louis to London for 14/18 October at stg 13.75.
Shipbrokers said this was a low rate as MSS achieved stg 14.25 on its last order for 14,250/14,500 tonnes.

Louis Dreyfus confirmed its fixture of 13,200 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santos or Paranagua to the Red Sea at 14/20 October at a rate rumoured to be around $40, which shipbrokers said was also on the low side.
New business included an inquiry from E D & F Man, which quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Paranagua to Algeria or the Black Sea for 4/12 October.
Genoc was open for 6,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Poland to Algeria for 7/11 October, shipbrokers said.
Elsewhere, Syria was reported to have bought 13,000 tonnes of raw sugar for November shipment although the name of the supplier has yet to emerge.
Syria also bought a cargo of white sugar from a European trade house, market sources said. -- Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
